    QUIC_SEND_FLAG_NONE                     = 0x0000,
    QUIC_SEND_FLAG_ALLOW_0_RTT              = 0x0001,   // Allows the use of encrypting with 0-RTT key.
    QUIC_SEND_FLAG_START                    = 0x0002,   // Asynchronously starts the stream with the sent data.
    QUIC_SEND_FLAG_FIN                      = 0x0004,   // Indicates the request is the one last sent on the stream.
    QUIC_SEND_FLAG_DGRAM_PRIORITY           = 0x0008,   // Indicates the datagram is higher priority than others.
    QUIC_SEND_FLAG_DELAY_SEND               = 0x0010,   // Indicates the send should be delayed because more will be queued soon.
    QUIC_SEND_FLAG_CANCEL_ON_LOSS           = 0x0020,   // Indicates that a stream is to be cancelled when packet loss is detected.
    QUIC_SEND_FLAG_PRIORITY_WORK            = 0x0040,   // Higher priority than other connection work.
    QUIC_SEND_FLAG_CANCEL_ON_BLOCKED        = 0x0080,   // Indicates that a frame should be dropped when it can't be sent immediately.
} QUIC_SEND_FLAGS;

Function table for MsQuic API version 2 containing pointers to all API entry points. Obtain via MsQuicOpenVersion/MsQuicOpen2.

functions.name: MsQuicOpenVersion
functions.signature: QUIC_STATUS QUIC_API MsQuicOpenVersion(uint32_t Version, const void** QuicApi);
functions.description: Opens/initializes the MsQuic API for the current process and returns a pointer to the API function table. Call this once (or maintain a reference count) and keep the returned table to invoke all other MsQuic entry points. When finished, release the reference with MsQuicClose.
requirements: Must be called at PASSIVE_LEVEL IRQL (per _IRQL_requires_max_(PASSIVE_LEVEL)).
Version must be a supported API version; current valid value is QUIC_API_VERSION_2 (2).
QuicApi must be a non-null pointer to writable storage for the returned function table pointer.
On success, caller must later pass the exact returned pointer to MsQuicClose to release the reference.
Caller must check the returned QUIC_STATUS and only use the API table if the call succeeds.
In 32-bit kernel mode, MsQuic is not supported; MsQuicOpenVersion will not be available (header maps to QUIC_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED).

functions.name: MsQuicClose
functions.description: Closes the MsQuic API handle previously returned by MsQuicOpenVersion/MsQuicOpen2 and releases the process’s reference to the API. After this call, the function table must not be used.
requirements: Must be called at PASSIVE_LEVEL IRQL (per _IRQL_requires_max_(PASSIVE_LEVEL)).
QuicApi must be the exact pointer previously returned by MsQuicOpenVersion/MsQuicOpen2.
Do not use the function table after calling MsQuicClose.
Each successful MsQuicOpenVersion/MsQuicOpen2 call should be balanced by a corresponding MsQuicClose.

functions.name: MsQuicOpen2
functions.description: Convenience helper for opening MsQuic at version 2. It calls MsQuicOpenVersion(QUIC_API_VERSION_2, ...) and returns the v2 QUIC_API_TABLE pointer. In C builds it may be a macro alias to MsQuicOpenVersion; in C++ it is an inline function.
requirements: Available as an inline function in C++ and as a macro in C; behavior is to invoke MsQuicOpenVersion with version 2.
QuicApi must be a non-null pointer to writable storage for a const QUIC_API_TABLE* result.
Caller must check the returned QUIC_STATUS and only use the table on success.
On success, the returned table pointer must later be passed to MsQuicClose to release the reference.
Subject to the same IRQL constraint as MsQuicOpenVersion (PASSIVE_LEVEL).
Not supported in 32-bit kernel mode environments (overall MsQuic not supported there).
